# Cases for the value of one query parameter. The Go decoder (internal/core) reads this file, and
# so does the codec of the browser (js/runtime/searchcodec.ts), run in Node and in beastjs. All must give
# the same answer for every line.
#
# Columns, separated by one tab:
#   type       string, bool, int, int8, int16, int32, int64, uint, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64, uintptr or
#              float (the type of the field, float is a float64: a float32 field is a build error)
#   input      the value as a JSON string
#   result     ok when the value is a number, bool or text the field takes, x when it is not
#   bits       for ok: the 64 bits of the decoded number as 16 hex digits, 1 or 0 for a bool, - for a string
#   canonical  for ok: the shortest text of the value as a JSON string, which the page is rendered for and
#              the address bar is rewritten to, - for x
#
# A whole number is digits with an optional + or -, and an optional point with zeros after it: +007, 1.0
# and -0 are accepted (-0 is 0). A float is digits with an optional sign, fraction and exponent: 010.50,
# .5, 5., 1e3. A whole number is in the range of its type and at most 2^53-1 in size, a float is 0 or
# between 1e-6 and 1e21 in size. No spaces, no hex, no NaN, no separators, no other digits than 0 to 9.
# A text of a number is at most 64 bytes long, whole numbers and floats alike: a longer one is not valid,
# since Go and the browser round a very long decimal differently. A bool is true or false only, a string
# is any text.
# What an empty value means (the field was not passed) is decided for the whole field, not here.
int	"0"	ok	0000000000000000	"0"
int	"-0"	ok	0000000000000000	"0"
int	"+0"	ok	0000000000000000	"0"
int	"00"	ok	0000000000000000	"0"
